problem_statement: The jekyll-doc-theme project site is a real Jekyll build served as a multi-page static docs site (a landing page at /index.html plus /docs/home/, /docs/themes/, and other docs pages that all share the top navigation and footer). A recent design change added a native 'Browse the docs' documentation index to the landing page (styled by assets/css/docs-outline.css and wired by assets/js/docs-status.js): a card grid of the theme's own docs pages (Home, Themes, Customization, Cheatsheet, Font Awesome, Bootstrap — sourced from the _data/docs.yml taxonomy), a section-filter chip row (All / Getting Started / Examples), and a live readout that reports 'Showing N of 6 · <section>' as the reader filters. The index was laid out as a fixed-width, non-wrapping flex row for both the chip row and the card grid, so it cannot shrink below its pinned width and the landing page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone while the desktop and tablet layouts still contain it. The same change was meant to promote a shared 'Browse the docs' footer mini-index into the site footer so it appears on every page (landing plus the docs pages), but in the shipped state the footer mini-index only renders on the landing page and is missing from the docs pages, and the section-filter readout does not track the chip that was clicked. Repair the doc index so the landing page fits a phone with no horizontal overflow, keep the shared footer mini-index present on every page, and keep the section-filter readout in sync with the active chip — preserving the paper-theme docs visual language, the original Jekyll homepage content, the three feature ideas, the docs taxonomy, and the bundled local images.
required_content: Repair the 'Browse the docs' doc-index (chip row + card grid) so the mobile (390px) landing page has no horizontal overflow (document scrollWidth within 24px of the viewport), while keeping the desktop and tablet layouts intact.

Keep all six doc cards visible (Home, Themes, Customization, Cheatsheet, Font Awesome, Bootstrap) with their real section tags (Getting Started / Examples) and the All / Getting Started / Examples filter chips.
Keep the shared 'Browse the docs' footer mini-index (labelled BROWSE THE DOCS) present in the footer of every page: the landing page AND the docs pages (/docs/home/, /docs/themes/).

Keep the section-filter control functional so its readout advances to the active section (for example 'Showing 3 of 6 · Getting Started') after a chip is clicked, not frozen on the initial 'Showing 6 of 6 · All sections'.

Preserve the original homepage content signals Jekyll Template for Project Websites, What is Jekyll?, Easy to install and publish, Modular Styling and Templating, Git-based source control, GitHub Pages, Markdown, Liquid, bootstrap-sass, and Bootwatch themes.
Keep the bundled local images assets/img/logonav.png and assets/img/jekyll-dark.png as browser-visible img elements with meaningful alt text.
Do not remove content, add a framework/package-manager/backend/remote API/remote image/new dependency, or introduce console or network errors.
The repair must be a scoped responsive-layout + wiring fix, not a content rewrite, and must not change the page content or DOM structure across viewports.
design_constraints: Fix the doc-index flex layout so the filter chips and doc cards wrap/flex fluidly on narrow viewports instead of pinning a fixed row width; use stable responsive constraints and normal media queries.

Keep the docs-theme visual language: clean top navigation, compact search affordance, restrained light cards on the paper theme, local logo, Font Awesome icons, and a clear documentation hierarchy. Do not restyle the index into a detached dark/off-palette panel or collapse the cards into an overlapping pile.
Render the shared 'Browse the docs' footer mini-index on every page's footer, not only the landing page, so the cross-page docs identity stays consistent.
Wire the section filter so the readout reflects the live count and section each time a chip is clicked; do not leave a stale readout that never updates.
Do not use viewport-width font scaling, hidden-only benchmark text, placeholder images, remote stock media, or overflow-x:hidden hacks that leave the underlying fixed-width row overflowing.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial verify the docs landing page loads across breakpoints with no horizontal overflow after the repair.

mobile_initial and mobile_docs_outline verify the repaired 'Browse the docs' index fits a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow; the original-with-defect leg overflows about 1015px and a shallow non-fix still overflows about 265px.

desktop_docs_outline and mobile_docs_outline verify the doc index keeps the paper-theme visual language (light cards, teal/indigo accents) and reads as a coherent docs card grid, not a detached dark panel or an overlapping card pile.
desktop_docs_status_after verifies the section-filter readout advances after a chip is clicked (interaction continuity).

desktop_docs_home, desktop_docs_themes, and mobile_docs_home verify the shared 'Browse the docs' footer mini-index is present on the docs pages, not only the landing page (cross-page design continuity).
desktop_feature_cards verifies the original three feature ideas remain visible; desktop_asset_regression verifies the local logo and Jekyll image remain browser-visible after the repair.

change_completion: The landing page shows the 'Browse the docs' index with all six doc cards, the section-filter chips, and the live count readout, plus the shared 'Browse the docs' footer mini-index.
The section-filter readout advances after a chip is clicked and the footer mini-index is present on the docs pages as well as the landing page.
design_consistency: The doc index and footer mini-index read as a coherent paper-theme docs design using clean navigation, light restrained cards, teal/indigo accents, local logo, and documentation hierarchy.
The index is not restyled into a detached dark/off-palette panel and the doc cards are not collapsed into an overlapping illegible pile.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile landing states have no horizontal overflow, clipped nav/search, overlapped hero text, or unstable card widths.
Mobile keeps the doc index readable in a wrapped single/multi-column rhythm with tappable filter chips.
regression: Original content signals for Jekyll, GitHub Pages, Markdown, Liquid, bootstrap-sass, Bootwatch themes, and the three feature ideas remain visible.
Bundled assets assets/img/logonav.png and assets/img/jekyll-dark.png remain browser-visible and no remote media or new dependencies are introduced.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a scoped design-continuity repair of the real Jekyll docs site: it makes the 'Browse the docs' index (chip row + doc-card grid) wrap/flex so the 390px mobile landing page has no horizontal overflow, keeps the index on the paper-theme visual language, keeps the shared footer mini-index present on every page (landing plus docs pages), and keeps the section-filter readout in sync with the active chip, while preserving the original project/docs content, taxonomy, local images, and desktop/tablet layouts. Leaving the fixed-width non-wrapping rows (baseline) or a shallow narrowing with overflow-x:hidden that still overflows the phone and collapses the cards into an off-palette dark pile while dropping the cross-page mini-index and freezing the readout (bad) fails multiple gates: no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, dom_assertions (cross-page mini-index), and interaction_assertions (stale readout).
author_notes: Slot 307 targets aksakalli/jekyll-doc-theme for docs / Design Continuity / repair / page, hardened to L4. The site is a real Jekyll build (jekyll build -> _site) served as a multi-page static docs site. The native lever is the theme's own docs taxonomy (_data/docs.yml) surfaced as a 'Browse the docs' card index with a section filter and a live count readout. Four orthogonal levers: (D6) fixed-width non-wrapping chip/card rows cause mobile horizontal overflow; (D3) the bad leg collapses the doc cards with negative margins into an off-palette near-black overlapping pile; (D2) the shared 'Browse the docs' footer mini-index is dropped from the docs pages; (D4) the section-filter readout is frozen by a stale closure. The reference repair fixes all four; the baseline fails D6/D3/D2 but passes D4; the bad leg fails all four. Content and DOM are identical across all legs (index.html is byte-identical); only the graded stylesheet, wiring JS, footer include, and the per-leg mini-index flag differ.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: An unused documentation-theme project that builds cleanly with a local Jekyll toolchain into a multi-page static docs site with shared navigation/footer, local docs images, and a docs taxonomy, making it a natural L4 docs design-continuity repair with cross-page, visual, interaction, and responsive levers.
